reproduction_target: BMDD (BiModal Dirichlet Distribution) R package: variational-EM imputation of zero-inflated microbiome compositional data, evaluated via parametric + non-parametric simulations (CDI/IBD/RA/SMOKE templates), benchmarked against competing imputation methods (mbDenoise, mbImpute, SAVER, scImpute, ALRA, DMM), and applied to a real CRC dataset with downstream differential-abundance analysis (LinDA).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods/Abstract prose + repo README (prose only, no workflow source read). Pure-computational: no wet-lab steps (W=0). Simulation and benchmarking detail lives in Supplementary Materials (not fetched at stage-1).

steps.label: BMDD core imputation: variational-EM estimation of bimodal Dirichlet mixture priors, posterior-mean composition estimates + multiple posterior samples (R package, install_github)
Simulation studies: parametric settings + non-parametric settings S6-S9 using four real datasets (CDI, IBD, RA, SMOKE) as templates (settings detailed in Supplementary A1.2)
Benchmark comparison against competing imputation methods: mbDenoise, mbImpute, SAVER, scImpute, ALRA, DMM (external packages, no versions or install info given)
Downstream differential-abundance analysis with ANCOMBC, MaAsLin, and LinDA (LinDA available via MicrobiomeStat; no package versions pinned)

Real-data application: zero-imputation of a colorectal-cancer microbiome dataset (Yu et al. 2017) followed by LinDA to identify disease-associated taxa (worked example shipped in README, deps phyloseq + MicrobiomeStat)
